audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Camille four of seven stages including '2+ items', and every prose field says the same — 'Two-plus items this is your matchup', 'the sidelane becomes your kingdom'. The Emerald+ number is 47.42% over 1200 games. A lane Camille loses by two and a half points is written as one she owns outright from first item onward.
audit.why: 1200 games is the second-largest sample in this slice, so the number is not noise. Zaahen's kit also argues against the late-game claim: Cultivation of War banks Determination stacks that give him permanent bonus attack damage and, at full stacks, a revive — a scaling passive with a second life is not something a burst duellist out-scales in a side lane. I have not flipped the chart, because I cannot verify from the kits alone which stage the deficit actually lives in, and inventing a power shift is worse than leaving a defensible one. Flagged for the user instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cultivation of War is absent from the entire matchup, in both layers. Nothing tells the reader that Zaahen banks stacks, gains attack damage from them, or revives at full stacks.
audit.why: A revive is the single most decision-changing thing in any kit that has one — it decides whether a level-6 all-in is a kill or a trade, whether to commit a 140s ultimate, and whether the side-lane duel the late section recommends is winnable at all. Riot's text: 'Zaahen's attacks and abilities against enemy champions grant him stacks of Determination, gaining bonus Attack Damage per stack. When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive.' Note the trigger — stacks come from hitting CHAMPIONS, so the fill rate is set by how much you let him touch you, which makes short trades a resource decision and not just a health one.
audit.corrected: Cultivation of War named at level 1 and level 6, with the stack-from-champion-hits mechanic and the revive stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Zaahen ability is named anywhere in either layer. The content layer uses 'his Q-E burst' and 'his ult'. The full layer is worse: it uses the literal placeholder word 'Ultimate' as if it were the ability's name — 'punish his Ultimate cooldown', 'Zaahen wins by landing Ultimate', 'only take a wall trade when Zaahen's Ultimate is down', 'keep E held until Ultimate is committed'. Camille's own R is written as 'Ultimatum' rather than The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.why: Riot's kit is Cultivation of War (P), The Darkin Glaive (Q, 10s — a double slash that heals him, recastable for a knockup), Dreaded Return (W, 14s — a stab that pulls enemies toward him), Aureate Rush (E, 10s — a dash with damage that scales on maximum health), and Grim Deliverance (R, 110s — a rise-and-slam that heals him for part of the damage). Four separate placeholder instructions point at 'his Ultimate' as the thing to bait before engaging, but Grim Deliverance is a 110s damage-and-heal, not a lockdown — the ability that actually punishes a Camille who commits is Dreaded Return, a 14s pull. The full layer is currently telling the reader to wait out the wrong cooldown by a factor of eight.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named; Grim Deliverance described as the 110s heal it is; Dreaded Return's 14s pull identified as the cooldown that actually gates the engage; Aureate Rush's max-health scaling stated; Camille's R given its full name.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Punish his whiffed cooldowns' and 'punish whiffed Hookshots' are the entire cooldown section — no ability and no duration on either side.
audit.why: The numbers make the lane legible and they are favourable in a way nothing in the text conveys: The Darkin Glaive is 10s, Aureate Rush is 10s and Dreaded Return is 14s, all against Hookshot's 16s. Every one of his tools comes back faster than her engage, which is the real reason the early game is a discipline contest rather than a window she can force — exactly what the prose is groping at when it says 'the lane is about mistakes'.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into early, mid and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal cue anywhere, in a matchup whose enemy heals off two separate abilities.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance sustain for this pairing. Both heal him, one on a 10s cooldown, and the matchup's own plan is to win extended duels in the side lane after Trinity Force — which is precisely the fight anti-heal decides.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds cue added to late.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json generates a line claiming Camille's Hookshot 'shuts off Zaahen's Aureate Rush'.
audit.why: That line is produced from a derived 'terrain' flag on Hookshot. Riot's own description is 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing' — it creates no terrain and applies no grounding, so there is no mechanism by which it denies his dash. I did not write it.

notes: This matchup was the thinnest in the slice and the full layer contained a placeholder that had shipped as content: the literal word 'Ultimate' is used as Zaahen's ability name in four places, including two instructions to hold Camille's engage until 'Ultimate is down'. His ultimate is Grim Deliverance, a 110s damage-and-heal — not a lockdown — so those lines were pointing the reader at a cooldown eight times longer than the one that actually punishes her engage (Dreaded Return, 14s). Cultivation of War was absent from both layers entirely, which means nothing told the reader that Zaahen banks attack damage off every hit he lands on a champion and REVIVES at full stacks; that single fact changes whether a level-6 all-in or a side-lane duel is worth taking. CHART CONCERN, not actioned: the lane is 47.42% over 1200 games but the chart and all three prose fields give Camille the game from first item onward. I did not flip it — see questionsForUser.
